v1.feedback: The cartwheel concept lands — a full 360° rotation on a timed cycle is a legit 'surprise swerve' off a Lorenz parent, and the teal flash at the apex is restrained enough to not feel gimmicky. The indigo→magenta→gold palette is attractive and the form reads instantly as a butterfly attractor. Two things to push: the 11s cycle feels slightly too frequent — after three flips it becomes predictable rather than delightful, try 18-25s with slight randomization so each cartwheel re-earns its surprise. The centrifugal puff (0.8 scale) is subtle on screen; consider adding a slight spiral trail or brief afterimage during the flip so the rotation reads as kinetic rather than just a rigid-body spin of the same cloud.

v2.feedback: The Lorenz attractor itself is unchanged — same sigma/rho/beta, same initial conditions, same integration step. The 'cartwheel' idea lands only as an extrinsic whole-scene rotation around X every ~18s with a teal flash at apex, which reads more like a turntable gimmick than a structural swerve. The ghost-trail mechanic is a nice touch but ghostPoints.visible is set false and only enabled during the cartwheel window, so for most of the runtime you're watching the exact same parent piece. To earn the 'surprise' mode: actually mutate the attractor (e.g. smoothly interpolate rho/sigma mid-flight to deform the butterfly into a different basin), or cartwheel individual lobes independently so the form itself tumbles rather than the camera.
